chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribaat, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far or Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the boy is breast-fed from various women, so that it constitutes a number, or his flesh and blood grow upon it, the daughters of all of them become prohibited to him.

key_terms.عِدَّةً: a number (referring to the count of feeds)

ai.seo_question: Does breastfeeding from multiple women create a prohibition with all of them?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the extent of the mahram relationship by establishing that sufficient nursing (radh') by multiple women creates a permanent prohibition for the boy against all their daughters, mirroring the bond of consanguinity. Shia jurists utilize this to define the criteria for 'radh''—whether through a specific count of feeds or the physical nourishment of flesh and blood—thereby extending the scope of marriage prohibitions beyond immediate maternal lines. This ruling underscores the theological view that milk kinship (qarabat al-radha') functions as a distinct legal category equivalent to blood lineage in Islamic family law.
